text:
Elaine (prod): Quick Q — we got a flood of asks this week: several enterprise customers pushing for reserved capacity + fine-grained quotas; a few startups asking for PAYG with burst credits. How should we prioritize these pricing/packaging items for Q3? :thinking:
Marco (pm): +1. Need a repeatable framework. I usually default to RICE for product decisions but we should map to revenue predictability & ops cost too.
Priya (sales): For context — 2 fintechs will only sign with reserved (compliance + SLA). 3 mid-market PLG customers would upgrade faster if burst credits exist.
Sam (eng): Engineering perspective: building full dedicated/reserved capacity support (routing, billing hooks, UI) looks like ~5 sprint-weeks + infra changes. Burst credits/hybrid throttling is smaller: ~2 sprint-weeks.
Jordan (finance): Reserved = better ARR visibility but longer deal cycles. Burst credits = faster conversion, lower short-term revenue. Also watch unit economics on tokens.
Casey (devex): Launch criteria we should insist on: (a) canary with 2 customers, (b) telemetry for per-route cost, (c) rollout plan with auto-fallback to PAYG.
Marco (pm): Proposed prioritization matrix: R (reach = number of customers affected), I (impact = revenue/retention), C (confidence), E (effort in sprint-weeks). Let's sketch 2 options with rough scores.
Sam (eng):```\n# quick RICE sketch\nReservedCapacity: Reach=2, Impact=8, Confidence=0.7, Effort=20 (dev-hours -> 5 sprints)\nBurstCredits: Reach=6, Impact=5, Confidence=0.8, Effort=8 (2 sprints)\n```
Marco (pm): Calculated scores (rough): Reserved ~ (2*8*0.7)/20 = 0.56, Burst ~ (6*5*0.8)/8 = 3.0. So by vanilla RICE burst wins.
Priya (sales): RICE is useful but misses strategic deals — those 2 fintechs are enterprise logo plays and could justify bespoke work.
Jordan (finance): Agreed. Maybe add a multiplier for strategic value (logo, upsell potential). That would bump Reserved.
Casey (devex): Also factor ops risk. Reserved introduces isolation & scheduling complexity — needs SRE validation. Risk multiplier?
Sam (eng): Neutral proposal: do a two-track plan — implement BurstCredits broadly (lower effort, higher RICE), and run a scoped Reserved pilot for the two fintechs (custom onboarding + dedicated lanes). That reduces overall risk and unlocks near-term conversions.
Elaine (prod): I like two-track. Questions: what are minimal acceptance criteria for the pilot? Who will own? timeline?
Casey (devex): Pilot acceptance: deployable in VPC/dedicated pool, canary traffic with prefixed routing, per-customer cost telemetry, rollback within 15m.
Marco (pm): Owners: Marco -> product lead for packaging; Sam -> eng lead for burst + pilot infra; Priya -> customer liaison for the fintech onboarding; Jordan -> finance for pricing terms.
Priya (sales): Customer ask: fintechs want a 12m reserved commit with SLA and ability to use burst credits for traffic spikes. We should prototype allowed burst credit usage on reserved customers.
Sam (eng): Implementation note: simplest approach for pilot: reuse existing dedicated pools, add per-customer quota config + billing flag. Avoid big UI work for pilot.
Jordan (finance): Pricing idea for pilot: 10% discount on committed spend vs PAYG, with pool-level overage billed at PAYG rates. That keeps revenue predictable but avoids complex credits accounting.
Marco (pm): Next steps: 1) scope PRD for BurstCredits MVP (wk1) 2) scope Reserved pilot PRD (wk1) 3) engineering spike for reserved routing (1 week) 4) finance to model ARR impact (2 days).
Elaine (prod): Meeting to align: 30m tomorrow 10:00am. Bring a short RICE table + call out any strategic multipliers you want applied.
ops-bot: Reminder: scheduled product-sync meeting in 24 hours (link: https://notion.example/xxx) :bell:
Sam (eng): I'll put a short spike branch up today and tag @Marco and @Casey.
Marco (pm): Great — if burst goes in first we can use it as a gating metric for signups -> measure conversion uplift.
Priya (sales): I'll line up the fintech legal points and check if they accept the simple overage model.
Jordan (finance): I'll run a sensitivity with 3 scenarios (fast conversion, medium, slow) and share numbers before the meeting.
Elaine (prod): Thanks everyone. Agreed: prioritize BurstCredits for broad rollout, Reserved as targeted pilot for strategic enterprise. We'll reconvene after spikes. :thumbsup:
